name: Complete daily hazard assessments and toolbox talks
summary: Before each shift the foreman of every self-perform crew walks the work area, writes a field level hazard assessment (FLHA) listing the day's tasks, hazards and controls, gets any work permits the tasks need, and holds a short toolbox talk where the crew reads and signs the form. During the day the foreman updates the form when the work or the weather changes, and at the end of the shift hands it in on paper or through a tablet app. Site safety coordinators file the forms, spot-check a sample and coach foremen whose forms are copied from the day before or too generic to be useful. The process is slow mostly because paper forms wait in site trailers to be keyed or scanned, and weak because repetitive work tempts foremen to copy yesterday's form.

baseline.org_archetype: A national Canadian general contractor with about 135 self-perform concrete, finishing and carpentry crews on about 220 active projects, holding COR certification in each province.
baseline.notes: Covers the company's own crews. Subcontractor crews complete their own employer's hazard assessments, which the safety coordinator also sees on site but which are not counted as cases here.

trigger: A self-perform crew arrives at the site at the start of a shift with the day's work plan.
end_state: The day's FLHA is signed by the crew, closed out at the end of the shift, filed in the safety system and either spot-checked, reviewed or used to coach the foreman.

volume.seasonality: Peaks from May to October when all crews work and overtime shifts are common; drops by about a quarter from December to February when some concrete crews are laid off.

evidence.note: About 135 crews (75 concrete, 25 finishing and 35 carpentry crews in the organisation file's resources) times about 21.7 working days a month gives about 2,930 crew-days, in line with the process map.

Foreman touch time of about 72 minutes per crew-day times about 2,900 crew-days a month at 130 productive hours. Common COR practice in Canadian construction: supervisors complete a field level hazard assessment each shift and the safety coordinator reviews a sample.
Person-minutes of crew members in the toolbox talk and sign-off for concrete-division crews (about 74% of crew-days).
Person-minutes of crew members in the toolbox talk and sign-off for carpentry and general crews (about 26% of crew-days), plus setting up permit controls.
Keying paper forms, spot checks, detailed reviews and coaching; about 13 minutes per crew-day on average.
Issues hot work, excavation and confined space permits for about a quarter of crew-days.
Handles repeat FLHA quality problems escalated by coordinators.

systems.name: Safety management system (hazard assessments, inspections, incidents, training records)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)

resources.name: Concrete and formwork crews (foreman plus 6 to 12 trades)
Telehandlers, skid steers and aerial work platforms

steps.name: Review work plan and site safety plan
steps.description: The foreman reads the day's work plan from the superintendent, the site safety plan and yesterday's FLHA for the same area, and notes which tasks, trades and equipment will be working near the crew.

evidence.note: Common COR practice in Canadian construction: supervisors complete a field level hazard assessment each shift and the safety coordinator reviews a sample.

steps.name: Walk the work area
steps.description: Before the crew starts, the foreman walks the deck, wall or room where the crew will work and looks for open edges, floor openings, overhead loads, energised services, poor footing, weather damage and work by other trades above or below.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 s.7(1) and the company COR program: assess the site before work begins

evidence.note: Alberta OHS Code s.7 requires a written assessment before work begins and when work changes; s.8 requires worker involvement. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check weather and wind for the day's tasks
steps.description: The foreman checks the forecast and the site anemometer or crane wind reading, because high wind, lightning, heavy rain or extreme cold stop crane lifts, work at heights, concrete placement and some formwork tasks.

next.condition: weather stops part of the planned work

evidence.note: Share of crew-days with a weather hold at the start of shift is an estimate for Canadian building sites across seasons.

steps.name: Hold work and re-plan tasks for the weather
steps.description: The foreman stops the affected tasks, keeps the crew in the trailer or moves them to sheltered work, phones the superintendent to agree a revised task list and waits for the wind or rain to drop before writing the assessment.

control.basis: Company crane and work-at-heights procedures: wind and lightning limits

evidence.note: Weather holds of half an hour to a full morning are typical on Canadian sites; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Write the field level hazard assessment
steps.description: The foreman fills in the FLHA card or tablet form: each task, the hazards found on the walk, the controls such as guardrails, harness tie-off points and exclusion zones, the emergency muster point and the PPE required, and signs it.

error.defect_description: Form copied from the previous day or written generically, missing a hazard that changed overnight.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 s.7(2)-(3): written hazard assessment report with controls and date; COR element on hazard assessment

evidence.note: Alberta OHS Code s.7 requires a written assessment before work begins and when work changes; s.8 requires worker involvement. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether a permit or plan is needed
steps.description: The foreman checks the tasks against the site safety plan's permit list: hot work, confined space entry, excavation entry, energised equipment, critical crane lifts and work on a swing stage each need a signed permit or plan before starting.

error.defect_description: A task that needs a permit is started without one.

evidence.note: Share of crew-days with permit-required work is an estimate for concrete and carpentry work on commercial buildings.

steps.name: Issue the work permit
steps.description: The superintendent or assistant superintendent reads the FLHA and permit request, walks to the location if needed, checks that fire watch, gas testing, shoring or lift plan are in place and signs the permit with its time limit.

control.basis: Site safety plan permit-to-work procedure; O. Reg. 213/91 confined space and excavation provisions; Alberta OHS Code hot work and confined space parts

evidence.note: Superintendents sign permits in common Canadian GC practice; the wait reflects the superintendent being elsewhere on site at shift start.

steps.name: Set up permit controls
steps.description: A labourer sets up the controls the permit names: fire extinguisher and fire watch for hot work, barricades and signs for an exclusion zone, gas detector readings for a confined space, or a spotter for equipment near the work.

control.basis: Conditions of the signed work permit

evidence.note: Set-up time for barricades, fire watch and gas testing is an estimate.

steps.name: Hold the toolbox talk
steps.description: The foreman gathers the crew at the work area, reads out the FLHA tasks, hazards and controls, covers any permit conditions, adds a short topic from the safety talks manual and asks each worker about hazards they see.

control.basis: Company COR program: pre-shift toolbox talk recorded with attendance

evidence.note: IHSA describes five-minute supervisor safety talks recorded on a talk report form; crew size and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Concrete crew discusses and signs the assessment
steps.description: Each carpenter or finisher on the concrete crew listens to the talk, raises hazards from their own task, initials the FLHA card or taps sign-off on the tablet and confirms they know the muster point. Minutes are the crew's total person-minutes.

error.defect_description: A worker signs without reading or arrives late and is not briefed.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 s.8: involve affected workers in hazard assessment and controls

evidence.note: Crew of 6 to 12 trades for 8 to 15 minutes each; author's estimate.

steps.name: General crew discusses and signs the assessment
steps.description: Each labourer or carpenter on the general works crew listens to the talk, raises hazards from their own task, initials the FLHA and confirms PPE and the muster point. Minutes are the crew's total person-minutes.

error.defect_description: A worker signs without reading or arrives late and is not briefed.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 s.8: involve affected workers in hazard assessment and controls

evidence.note: Crew of 5 to 10 for 8 to 15 minutes each; author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm tickets, PPE and equipment pre-use checks
steps.description: The foreman checks that workers doing the day's tasks hold the needed training such as working at heights or elevated work platform cards, have the PPE listed on the FLHA, and that the telehandler and lift operators have done their pre-use inspections.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 and Ontario working at heights training requirements; manufacturer pre-use inspection of equipment

next.condition: a worker lacks training proof or is new to the site

evidence.note: Share of crew-days with a new or uncertified worker is an estimate driven by union hall dispatch turnover.

steps.name: Orient a new worker or verify training records
steps.description: The site safety coordinator gives the new worker the site-specific orientation, or looks up the worker's training records in the safety system and the union's records, and either clears the worker or reassigns them to tasks they are qualified for.

control.basis: Site safety plan: site-specific orientation before starting work; COR training element

evidence.note: Orientation length and coordinator response time are estimates.

steps.name: Monitor work and reassess when conditions change
steps.description: During the shift the foreman watches the crew's work and checks whether tasks, equipment, other trades or the weather have changed enough that the morning assessment no longer covers the hazards.

evidence.note: Code s.7(4) requires reassessment when work processes change; share of crew-days with a mid-shift change is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the assessment and re-brief the crew
steps.description: The foreman adds the new task or hazard and its controls to the FLHA, stops the crew for a short re-brief and collects initials from the workers affected.

error.defect_description: The change is briefed verbally but never written on the form.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 s.7(4): repeat the assessment when a work process changes

evidence.note: Alberta OHS Code s.7 requires a written assessment before work begins and when work changes; s.8 requires worker involvement. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close out the assessment at end of shift
steps.description: At the end of the shift the foreman records on the FLHA whether hazards remain open, whether anyone was hurt and any near misses, and signs the close-out section.

error.defect_description: Near miss left off the close-out section.

next.condition: a near miss or open hazard needs reporting

evidence.note: Common COR practice in Canadian construction: supervisors complete a field level hazard assessment each shift and the safety coordinator reviews a sample.

steps.name: Report a near miss or open hazard
steps.description: The foreman phones or messages the safety coordinator and superintendent, describes the near miss or hazard, and fills in the hazard or near miss report in the safety system so it can be investigated.

control.basis: Company incident and near miss reporting procedure

evidence.note: Share of crew-days with a reported near miss or hazard is an estimate.

steps.name: Hand in the form
steps.description: The foreman drops the paper FLHA in the trailer collection box or syncs the tablet form to the safety system, depending on whether the site has moved to the electronic form.

evidence.note: Split between paper and tablet forms in 2019-2022 is an estimate; many contractors adopted mobile FLHA apps during this period.

steps.name: Scan and index paper forms
steps.description: The safety coordinator collects the paper forms from the trailer box, scans them, names each file by date, crew and area and attaches it to the site's record in the safety system.

error.defect_description: Form filed under the wrong date or crew.

evidence.note: Coordinators typically collect forms each morning or a few times a week; times are estimates.

steps.name: Spot-check the form
steps.description: The safety coordinator opens the day's forms for the site, checks each has tasks, hazards, controls and crew signatures, and picks a sample, or any form that looks copied, for a closer review.

control.basis: COR audit: documented review of hazard assessments by supervisors and safety staff

evidence.note: COR audits check documentation; the sampling share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the form against the work done
steps.description: The safety coordinator compares the form with what the crew was actually doing that day, from photos, the daily report and a site walk, and checks whether hazards and controls are specific to the task or generic and copied.

control.basis: COR audit hazard assessment element: quality of field level hazard assessments

next.condition: form copied, generic or missing hazards

evidence.note: Share of sampled forms found deficient is an estimate; copied forms are a common complaint in COR audits.

steps.name: Coach the foreman
steps.description: On the next site visit the safety coordinator sits with the foreman, shows the weak form beside the actual work and agrees what a specific assessment would have said, then notes the coaching in the safety system.

evidence.note: Coaching time and repeat rate are estimates.

steps.name: Escalate a repeat problem
steps.description: The regional safety manager reviews the foreman's recent forms and coaching records, meets the general foreman, and decides on retraining, closer supervision or a written warning under the company's safety discipline policy.

control.basis: Company safety accountability and progressive discipline policy

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Weather hold at shift start
exceptions.description: Wind, lightning or heavy rain stops lifts or work at heights; the crew waits or is re-planned before the assessment is written.

exceptions.name: Permit-required work
exceptions.description: Hot work, confined space, excavation or critical lifts need a superintendent-signed permit and set-up controls before the talk.

exceptions.name: New or uncertified worker
exceptions.description: A worker dispatched from the union hall needs orientation or proof of training before starting.

exceptions.name: Copied or generic form
exceptions.description: A sampled form turns out to be copied from the day before; the foreman is coached and repeat cases go to the safety manager.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from crew arrival to the form being filed and checked in the safety system
benchmarks.population: Self-perform crews of a Canadian general contractor, 2019-2022

evidence.note: The on-site part takes one shift; the rest is the delay before paper forms are scanned and spot-checked. No published benchmark found.

benchmarks.population: Ontario construction supervisors using the IHSA safety talks manual

evidence.note: IHSA describes its talks as five-minute talks; actual talks with the FLHA read-out run 8 to 15 minutes in this file.

pain_points.description: Foremen copy the previous day's FLHA on repetitive deck and wall cycles, so the form misses hazards that changed overnight.

evidence.note: Common finding in COR audits and safety coordinator reviews; frequency is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Paper forms sit in trailer boxes for a day or more before scanning, so the office cannot see open hazards or trends until later.

evidence.note: Estimate based on paper-to-scan practice before mobile FLHA apps were widespread.

pain_points.description: Crews wait at shift start for a superintendent to sign permits, holding the whole crew idle.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Coordinators can review only a sample of about 2,900 forms a month, so most forms are filed without anyone reading them closely.

evidence.note: Follows from 45 coordinators and the monthly volume.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 2: Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control
sources.supports: s.7: assess the work site before work begins, prepare a written report with the controls and the date, repeat at reasonably practicable intervals and when work or processes change; s.8: involve affected workers in the assessment and the controls.

sources.title: Safety Talks Manual
sources.supports: 168 five-minute safety talks for supervisors and health and safety representatives; separate Safety Talk Report Form log book records subject, attendees and results as documentation that talks were delivered on site.

sources.title: COR Process
sources.supports: COR needs an external audit score of at least 80%, is valid three years with annual internal maintenance audits of at least 60%, and audits review documentation, interviews and observations.

assumptions: Ontario's O. Reg. 213/91 does not use the term field level hazard assessment; the company applies the same COR-based FLHA form in every province, and Alberta's OHS Code Part 2 is cited as the most explicit written requirement.
Concrete, finishing and formwork crew members are modelled with the carpenter role and carpentry and general crews with the labourer role; finishers are not split out.
Crew attendance at the talk is recorded as the crew's total person-minutes on one step, so the carpenter and labourer FTEs represent many workers each spending 10 to 15 minutes a day.
The superintendent signs permits; the organisation file's process entry does not list the superintendent or safety manager as roles.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage plus about 35 to 45% for benefits, union contributions and overhead as set there).
The validator's staffing check uses 130 productive hours a month; field roles work closer to 170 hours in season, so stated field FTEs are slightly high relative to headcount.
